intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech by wandering the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then stay for the magical transformation at dusk when food stalls fill the air with smoke and spices. Explore the labyrinthine souks of the old medina for handcrafted goods, leather, and spices.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Journey to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for a sunset camel trek into the Sahara. Spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, and wake at dawn to witness a breathtaking desert sunrise over the dunes.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's imperial past with a self-guided or local-guided tour of the stunning 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellige tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Then visit the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden necropolis of Moroccan sultans dating to the 16th century, rediscovered only in 1917.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a riad kitchen where a local chef guides you through preparing authentic Moroccan dishes such as lamb tagine, preserved lemon chicken, harira soup, and fresh msemen flatbread. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to hand-pick your ingredients before cooking.

experiences.name: Sandboarding on the Sahara Dunes
experiences.description: Get your adrenaline pumping by sandboarding down the towering red-gold dunes of Erg Chebbi. Local guides provide boards and instruction for both beginners and experienced riders. Combine with a quad bike ride across the desert flats for a full adventure morning before the midday heat sets in.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara

day_by_day.morning: No activities – flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities – flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a petit taxi (negotiate fare, approximately 50-70 MAD) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Grab a quick late-night snack near the riad if anything is still open, or rely on a convenience store near the medina.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near the hotel or a small 24-hour snack shop – look for a msemen (Moroccan flatbread) or harira soup stall (15-25 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy for the next day. Exchange some cash at the airport or an ATM (avoid airport exchange counters for best rates). Download offline maps of Marrakech medina before landing.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at a local café near the medina. Head to Djemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere – snake charmers, orange juice vendors, and storytellers begin their day early. Walk through the historic Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior viewing is free and stunning).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Marrakech Medina souks on foot – browse the spice market (Rahba Kedima), leather goods, lanterns, and textiles. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the most beautiful Islamic colleges in North Africa (entry ~20 MAD). Haggle for souvenirs; prices are very negotiable. Grab lunch at a local hole-in-the-wall restaurant in the medina.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at sunset when the square transforms into a massive open-air food festival. Try grilled meats, snail soup, and Moroccan bread from the food stalls (budget 40-60 MAD for a full dinner). Watch the entertainers, musicians, and acrobats – completely free. Return to the hotel on foot or by petit taxi.

meals.breakfast: Local café near the medina – café au lait, msemen, and honey (20-30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Hole-in-the-wall tagine restaurant inside the souks – chicken or vegetable tagine with bread (40-60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls – grilled kefta, Moroccan salad, and fresh orange juice (40-60 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – medina streets are cobblestone and narrow. Watch out for motorbikes in the alleys. Carry small change (coins) for tipping musicians or photographers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs, a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis hidden in the medina (entry ~70 MAD). Then walk to the El Badi Palace ruins – a massive 16th-century palace now open as a museum (entry ~70 MAD). The rooftop views over the medina and Atlas Mountains are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) to explore its historic architecture and the Lazama Synagogue (free or small donation). Visit the Bahia Palace, a 19th-century grand riad-style palace with ornate tilework and carved cedar ceilings (entry ~70 MAD). Take a slow walk through the quieter southern medina streets.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at a budget-friendly local restaurant in Mouassine neighborhood – try pastilla (savory-sweet pigeon pie) or a slow-cooked lamb tagine. Spend the evening browsing the night market at Djemaa el-Fna or relax at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery – fresh khobz bread, olive oil, and argan honey (20-30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Street food near El Badi Palace – merguez sandwich or a bowl of harira soup (20-35 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local Moroccan restaurant in Mouassine – pastilla or tagine with mint tea (60-80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Saadian Tombs can get crowded by mid-morning – arrive early. Bahia Palace is a short walk from the Mellah. All three major sites can be covered in one day on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (around 06:00–07:00) on a shared budget group tour to the Sahara Desert via Ouarzazate and the Draa Valley (book in advance through a local agency – 3-day/2-night shared tours start from ~900-1,200 MAD per person). Travel through the stunning High Atlas Mountains, stopping at Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m altitude) for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey through Ouarzazate – the 'Hollywood of Africa.' Brief stop at the famous Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in countless films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones (entry ~10 MAD). Explore the mud-brick kasbahs and climb for panoramic views. Continue driving south toward the Draa Valley.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zagora or Ouarzazate area for overnight stay at a budget guesthouse or auberge (included in group tour package). Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner under the stars – harira, tagine, and Moroccan mint tea around a communal fire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure (included or 20-30 MAD at a café)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or a roadside café stop near Tizi n'Tichka (40-60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included in tour package – traditional Berber communal dinner at guesthouse

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara group tour at least 1-2 days in advance from Djemaa el-Fna area agencies. Shared tours are the most budget-friendly option. Pack a light jacket – Atlas Mountain passes can be cold even in March. Bring a scarf/shemagh for desert wind.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and continue the drive to Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes – the iconic orange-red Sahara dunes reaching up to 150 meters high. Arrive by late morning. Check into a budget desert camp or auberge at the edge of the dunes. Take a short walk to the base of the dunes and explore the small Berber village of Merzouga.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mount a camel for a guided sunset camel trek into the Sahara dunes (included in most group tour packages or ~150-200 MAD separately). Trek 1-2 hours deep into the dunes. Arrive at a traditional Berber desert camp with nomad-style tents. Watch the golden hour light paint the dunes in breathtaking colors.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the night at a desert camp under a sky full of stars (minimal light pollution). Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner around a campfire with live music – Gnawa drums and singing. Stargaze from the top of a dune – one of the most memorable experiences in Morocco. Sleep in a nomad tent.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at guesthouse before departure (included in tour)
meals.lunch: Simple lunch at Merzouga village café – tagine or couscous (40-60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included in camp package – Berber dinner with tagine, salad, and mint tea around the fire

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat – the desert sun is intense even in March. Nights in the Sahara can drop to 5-10°C in March, so pack a warm layer. Protect your camera and phone from sand. This is the highlight of the trip – soak it all in.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 06:00) to climb the dunes and watch the Sahara sunrise – an absolutely magical experience. Take final photos of the golden dunes. Enjoy breakfast at camp, then begin the long return journey to Marrakech via a different scenic southern route through the Todra Gorge or Dades Valley (depending on tour itinerary).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the dramatic Todra Gorge – a 300-meter-high narrow canyon carved by the Todra River (free entry). Walk through the gorge, spot rock climbers, and enjoy the cool canyon air. Continue through the Valley of Roses (Kelaat M'Gouna) – in March, early roses may be blooming. Stop at a local cooperative to buy rose water or rose products at source prices.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by late evening (approximately 20:00-21:00). Drop bags at the hotel, freshen up, and head to Djemaa el-Fna for a final evening meal. Reflect on the desert adventure over a pot of Moroccan mint tea.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp – Moroccan bread, olive oil, jam, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at Todra Gorge – tagine or sandwich at a local café (40-60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls or a sit-down medina restaurant – brochettes, Moroccan salad, and fresh juice (50-70 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is long (8-10 hours with stops). Sleep in the vehicle when possible. The Todra Gorge stop is a highlight – budget at least 45-60 minutes there. Keep some MAD cash for roadside stops and tips for the driver/guide.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Marrakech. Visit the Majorelle Garden – a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent (entry ~70 MAD, Berber Museum inside ~30 MAD extra). The garden is beautiful in March with spring flowers. Walk through the upscale Gueliz neighborhood (Ville Nouvelle) for a different side of Marrakech.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souk shopping for last-minute souvenirs – argan oil, Moroccan spices, leather goods, or handmade ceramics. Visit the Mellah spice market for the best prices on saffron, ras el hanout, and cumin. Pack your bags, check out of the hotel, and store luggage if needed. Take a final walk around Djemaa el-Fna.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport with plenty of time. Take a petit taxi (50-70 MAD) or negotiate a private transfer. Enjoy one last glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice from a Djemaa el-Fna vendor before leaving – at 4 MAD it's the best budget farewell in Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at a medina café – baghrir (honeycomb pancakes) with argan honey and mint tea (25-35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near Majorelle Garden – a sandwich or salad in Gueliz (35-50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or a final street food snack before departure (40-60 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden opens at 08:00 – go early to avoid crowds. Keep airport transfer budget in mind. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if flying internationally. Exchange leftover MAD back to your currency at the airport (rates are acceptable for small amounts). Morocco will leave you wanting to come back!

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (~20-30 min by taxi or pre-arranged hotel shuttle). Check in, freshen up, and unwind. If hungry, ask the hotel for a light late-night snack or room service.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel or room service upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer before landing to avoid stress. Keep a small amount of Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) handy for tips and incidentals. Rest well – Day 2 is packed with exploration.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, head into the historic Medina. Begin with a visit to the stunning Koutoubia Mosque (exterior viewing) and the adjacent gardens. Walk to Djemaa el-Fna Square to soak in the morning atmosphere – snake charmers, orange juice vendors, and street performers are already active. Then explore the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully ornate 16th-century royal burial site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the opulent Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with intricate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, dive deep into the labyrinthine souks – explore the dyers' souk, spice market, leather goods, and lantern makers. Bargaining is expected and part of the experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna as the square transforms into a magical open-air spectacle with food stalls, musicians, storytellers, and acrobats. Dine at one of the rooftop terraces overlooking the square for an unforgettable atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – enjoy Moroccan staples like msemen (flatbread), honey, argan oil, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Café Arabe or a local souk café – try a tagine or harira soup (~80–120 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant on Djemaa el-Fna – try lamb kefta, couscous, or bastilla (pigeon pie) (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina's streets are cobblestone and uneven. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) out of respect for local culture. Keep your valuables secure in the souks.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a visit to the breathtaking Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD), a cobalt-blue botanical paradise once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the adjacent Berber Museum within the grounds. Afterward, stroll through the Gueliz (New City) neighborhood to see the blend of French colonial and Moroccan architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) – a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the ramparts. Then head to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) to explore its covered market and historic synagogue. In the late afternoon, treat yourself to a traditional Moroccan hammam experience at a mid-range local hammam (~200–300 MAD for a full scrub and massage).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in the Mouassine neighborhood – one of Marrakech's trendiest areas with boutique shops, art galleries, and excellent restaurants. Perfect for a slower-paced cultural evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riad restaurant near Majorelle Garden – fresh salads, grilled meats, and Moroccan pastries (~100–150 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riad restaurant in Mouassine neighborhood – try slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes and almonds (~150–200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book your hammam session in advance, especially for popular mid-range options like Les Bains de Marrakech. The Majorelle Garden gets crowded midday – arriving early is recommended. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (~18–24°C), ideal for garden visits.

day_by_day.date: 2027-03-18 (Drive to the Sahara – High Atlas & Draa Valley)
day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 7:00–7:30 AM) from Marrakech by private driver or shared tour toward the Sahara Desert (~8–9 hours total drive to Merzouga). Cross the magnificent High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka Pass (2,260m elevation) – stop for photos of the dramatic mountain scenery and Berber villages. Visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou Kasbah (entry ~10 MAD), a stunning fortified mud-brick city used as a filming location for Game of Thrones and Gladiator.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Rose Valley (Vallée des Roses) near Kelaat M'Gouna, famous for its damask rose cultivation (peak bloom in May, but the valley is scenic year-round). Pass through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') and continue east through the dramatic Draa Valley with its ancient kasbahs, palm groves, and ochre landscapes. Stop for a roadside lunch in Ouarzazate.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga (~18:00–19:00). Mount camels for a 45-minute sunset ride into the Sahara Desert to your desert camp. Watch the sun dip below the dunes in one of the most spectacular sunsets on Earth. Settle into your mid-range desert camp (traditional Berber tents with proper beds and en-suite facilities).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure – pack snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Ouarzazate – couscous, tagine, or grilled meats (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp under the stars – harira soup, tagine, Moroccan salads, and mint tea (~included in most camp packages or ~200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book your private driver or a guided tour in advance for this route. The drive is long but incredibly scenic – bring a camera. Dress in layers as desert temperatures drop significantly after sunset (can reach 5–10°C at night in March). The camel ride is included in most desert camp packages.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (~5:30 AM) for a magical sunrise over the Erg Chebbi dunes – arguably the most awe-inspiring moment of the trip. Watch the golden light paint the sand in shades of orange and red. After breakfast at camp, explore the dunes on foot or try sandboarding down the slopes (boards available at camp or nearby rental shops, ~50–100 MAD). Visit the nearby village of Merzouga to interact with the local Berber community and see traditional crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a 4x4 desert excursion through the surrounding desert landscape – visit a nomadic Berber family in their traditional tent, see the fossil-rich black rock desert (Hamada), and explore the seasonal Dayet Srji lake (when filled, it attracts pink flamingos). Alternatively, rent quad bikes for a thrilling desert adventure (~300–400 MAD/hour). Return to camp for a relaxing afternoon and optional camel ride.
day_by_day.evening: As darkness falls, the Sahara reveals its most extraordinary gift – a sky absolutely ablaze with stars, far from any light pollution. Enjoy a stargazing session with your camp guide pointing out constellations and the Milky Way. Share stories around a campfire with fellow travelers to the sound of Berber Gnawa music played by local musicians.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the desert camp – Moroccan bread, eggs, honey, argan oil, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at the camp or in Merzouga village – tagine or grilled meats (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Another traditional Berber dinner at camp under the stars – often includes a tajine feast and fresh Moroccan salads

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf/buff to protect against sand and sun. Stay hydrated – the desert air is very dry. The quad biking and 4x4 excursions should be booked through your camp or a local operator in Merzouga. Nights can be cold (5–10°C) – bring a warm layer.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for one final sunrise over the dunes. After breakfast, depart the desert camp by camel back to the road (~45 min). Begin the return journey toward Marrakech via a different northern route for variety. Drive through the spectacular Ziz Gorges and the lush Ziz Valley – a stunning river valley lined with thousands of palm trees cutting through dramatic rocky canyon landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pass through the mountain town of Midelt, known as the 'capital of apples' and a great place to stop for lunch and browse local carpet and fossil vendors. Continue through the cedar forests of the Middle Atlas near Azrou, where wild Barbary macaque monkeys roam freely along the roadside – a delightful and unexpected wildlife encounter. Continue driving toward Marrakech.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech in the late evening (~20:00–21:00). Check back into Aegean Bliss Resort. Freshen up and enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel to decompress after the long but rewarding journey.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the desert camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Midelt – try mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) or a hearty Berber tagine at a local restaurant (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant near the hotel in Marrakech – keep it light with a Moroccan salad platter and grilled chicken (~120–160 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return route via Midelt and Azrou is longer (~10 hours) but more scenic and less traveled than the outbound route. The Barbary macaque stop near Azrou is a highlight – however, avoid feeding the monkeys. Confirm your private driver is comfortable with this northern return route when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed final morning. Head to the vibrant Mellah spice market for last-minute souvenir shopping – saffron, argan oil, ras el hanout spice blends, and Moroccan ceramics make wonderful gifts. Visit the beautiful Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with intricate geometric tilework, carved stucco, and a peaceful central courtyard – one of Marrakech's most photogenic historic sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a final leisurely lunch in the Medina. Spend the early afternoon at a rooftop café with views over the rooftops of Marrakech, sipping mint tea and reflecting on the journey. Return to the hotel to pack, shower, and prepare for departure. Depending on your outbound flight time, arrange your airport transfer with the hotel concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Marrakech – if time permits before your departure, revisit Djemaa el-Fna one last time for its electric evening atmosphere. Say goodbye to the sights, sounds, and scents of Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – enjoy a final Moroccan breakfast spread
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a Medina restaurant – try a classic Moroccan pastilla or a mezze-style shared spread (~120–160 MAD)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the airport or early dinner near the hotel before departure – depending on flight schedule

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in at Marrakech Menara Airport. Keep some Dirhams for tips, last-minute purchases, and airport snacks. Exchange any remaining Dirhams back to your home currency at the airport (MAD cannot be exported in large quantities). This is a wonderful trip – cherish every memory of Morocco's magic!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities – flight UA arrives at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from Marrakech Menara Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in a chauffeured Mercedes-Benz S-Class or similar. Upon arrival, enjoy a warm welcome with traditional Moroccan mint tea and rose water hand ceremony. Check in and settle into your premium beachfront suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities – travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night light welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Unwind with a glass of Moroccan wine or freshly squeezed orange juice on your private terrace. Early rest recommended to prepare for the immersive days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable – travel day
meals.lunch: Not applicable – in transit
meals.dinner: In-resort late-night dining: Moroccan mezze platter, harira soup, and slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemons and olives, served in the resort's candlelit restaurant or via private in-suite dining.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30 – no activities are scheduled before check-in. Ensure your resort pre-arranges VIP airport meet-and-greet service and fast-track assistance. Confirm luggage handling and suite readiness in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a gourmet breakfast at the resort. At 10:00 AM, embark on a private guided tour of the iconic Jemaa el-Fna Square in the heart of Marrakech's medina. Explore the vibrant souks of the medina with a personal expert guide – discover the spice market (Souk des Épices), the leather tanneries, and artisan workshops producing hand-crafted lanterns, carpets, and zellige tilework.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the magnificent Bahia Palace, a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture with ornate carved cedar ceilings, mosaic courtyards, and lush gardens. Continue to the Saadian Tombs, a hidden necropolis dating to the 16th century, rediscovered in 1917. Enjoy a private guided tour of both sites with historical context from your expert guide. Stop for a refreshing mint tea break at a traditional riad café.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a rooftop terrace overlooking the medina and Atlas Mountains. Dinner at a top-tier Marrakech restaurant such as Le Foundouk or Dar Yacout – a theatrical multi-course Moroccan feast featuring bastilla (pigeon pastilla), slow-braised lamb with ras el hanout, and honey-drenched pastilla dessert in a stunning riad setting with live Gnawa music.

meals.breakfast: Lavish resort buffet with Moroccan msemen flatbreads, amlou (argan oil and almond spread), fresh fruit, pastries, eggs to order, and freshly squeezed juices.
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at a rooftop riad restaurant in the medina – grilled kefta brochettes, zaalouk (smoky eggplant salad), and freshly baked khobz bread.
meals.dinner: Premium Moroccan fine dining at Dar Yacout or Le Foundouk – multi-course tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring bastilla, lamb tagine, and traditional Moroccan pastries.

day_by_day.notes: Book Bahia Palace and Saadian Tombs tickets in advance to avoid queues. Arrange private medina guide through the resort concierge. Dress modestly for cultural sites – lightweight layers recommended for March weather.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, visit the Majorelle Garden – the iconic cobalt-blue botanical masterpiece originally created by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the lush gardens filled with exotic cacti, bamboo groves, and vivid blue pavilions. Visit the adjacent Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech (MYSLM) – a world-class museum celebrating the legendary designer's lifelong love affair with Morocco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience a private hammam and spa ritual at one of Marrakech's most prestigious wellness sanctuaries – La Mamounia Spa or the resort's own luxury spa. Enjoy a traditional black soap (beldi) scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. This 2-hour ritual is quintessentially Moroccan and deeply restorative.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset horse-drawn carriage (caleche) ride along the ramparts of the ancient medina walls, illuminated at dusk. Dinner at La Mamounia's Le Marocain restaurant or a similarly prestigious establishment – expect impeccable service, fine Moroccan cuisine, and a setting of unrivaled grandeur.

meals.breakfast: À la carte resort breakfast – Moroccan crêpes (meloui), honey, argan oil, soft-boiled eggs, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort or a chic café near Majorelle Garden – Moroccan salads, grilled vegetable skewers, and fresh lemonade with orange blossom water.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at La Mamounia's Le Marocain or equivalent – royal couscous with seven vegetables, slow-cooked mechoui lamb, and traditional Moroccan sweets with mint tea ceremony.

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden requires advance ticket booking, especially in peak season. La Mamounia Spa reservations should be made at least 48 hours ahead. The caleche ride is best arranged through the concierge for a private, curated experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech at 07:00 AM in a luxury 4x4 vehicle (Land Rover Defender or similar) with a private driver-guide for the scenic journey to the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley. En route, stop at the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) through the High Atlas Mountains – a breathtaking drive with panoramic views of snow-dusted peaks and Berber villages clinging to cliffsides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the ancient kasbahs of Aït Benhaddou – a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Morocco's most spectacular earthen fortresses, used as a backdrop for films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Enjoy a private guided tour of the ksar (fortified village) with a local historian. Lunch at a traditional Kasbah restaurant overlooking the site.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Merzouga by late afternoon. Check in to a luxury desert camp (such as Scarabeo Camp or Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp) – private Berber-style tents with en-suite bathrooms, plush furnishings, and stargazing terraces. At sunset, mount camels for a guided golden-hour camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes. Watch the Saharan sunset paint the dunes in amber and crimson. Dinner under the stars at the camp with live Berber music around a fire.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure – grab-and-go Moroccan pastry box prepared by the resort for the road.
meals.lunch: Traditional Moroccan lunch at a kasbah restaurant near Aït Benhaddou – lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, fresh salads, and Moroccan bread.
meals.dinner: Authentic Berber feast at the luxury desert camp – mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), couscous, Saharan salads, and fresh fruit, served under a canopy of Sahara stars with Gnawa drumming.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours including stops. Depart early to maximize daylight. Pack sunscreen, sunglasses, a light scarf for the dunes, and a warm layer for the cool desert evening. Confirm luxury camp reservations well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private sunrise hot-air balloon flight over the Erg Chebbi dunes – one of the most extraordinary experiences in the Sahara. Drift silently above the rippling sea of orange sand as the sun rises over the Algerian border. Upon landing, enjoy a Champagne breakfast in the dunes. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast and optional sandboarding on the mega-dunes with a guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Merzouga region with your private guide – visit a traditional nomadic Berber family encampment for an authentic cultural exchange, learn about desert survival techniques, and browse hand-woven Berber carpets and silver jewelry. Optional quad biking adventure across the dunes for an adrenaline-fueled desert experience. Relax at the camp's private pool (if available) or enjoy a desert spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Second night at the luxury desert camp. Enjoy a private stargazing session with a telescope and expert astronomer guide – the Sahara offers some of the clearest, darkest skies on Earth, perfect for viewing the Milky Way and constellations. Nightcap of Moroccan herbal tea by the fire before retiring to your sumptuous desert tent.

meals.breakfast: Champagne and gourmet breakfast in the dunes post-balloon flight – pastries, fresh fruit, artisan cheeses, and Moroccan mint tea. Full camp breakfast upon return.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the camp or a nearby traditional Berber restaurant – harira soup, Moroccan flatbreads, and a slow-cooked desert tagine.
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the desert camp – grilled meats, Moroccan vegetable dishes, and a selection of Saharan-inspired desserts with dates and honey.

day_by_day.notes: Hot-air balloon flights are weather-dependent and must be booked in advance. Confirm availability with the operator before departure from Marrakech. Bring a warm jacket for the pre-dawn balloon launch – desert temperatures drop significantly overnight in March.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the desert camp at 08:00 AM and begin the return journey toward Marrakech via the scenic northern route through the Ziz Valley and Todra Gorge. Stop at the spectacular Todra Gorge – a dramatic canyon with sheer 300-meter rock walls carved by the Todra River. Take a guided walk through the gorge floor, passing Berber villages and date palm oases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the verdant Dadès Valley – known as the 'Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs' – stopping to photograph the iconic Aït Benhaddou kasbah once more from a different vantage point if time permits. Visit the rose-growing village of Kelaat M'Gouna, famous for its annual Rose Festival and the production of premium Moroccan rose water and rose oil (argan-rose beauty products make excellent luxury souvenirs). Arrive in Ouarzazate – the 'Hollywood of Africa' – for a brief visit to Atlas Film Studios.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at a luxury boutique hotel in Ouarzazate (such as Berbère Palace or Dar Kamar) or continue to a riad en route. Enjoy a relaxing dinner at the hotel's restaurant, reflecting on two extraordinary days in the Sahara.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast – Moroccan porridge (asida), fresh dates, argan oil, and mint tea before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Tinghir near Todra Gorge – freshly made tagine, Berber bread, and seasonal salads.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Ouarzazate hotel restaurant or a recommended local establishment – slow-cooked lamb with preserved lemons, saffron-infused couscous, and pastilla dessert.

day_by_day.notes: The return journey covers approximately 6–7 hours of driving including stops. Pace the day comfortably with your private driver. Rose water and rose oil products from Kelaat M'Gouna are among Morocco's finest luxury souvenirs – budget time for shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Return drive to Marrakech (approximately 3.5 hours from Ouarzazate), arriving mid-morning. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a final leisurely morning. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins – a 16th-century sultan's palace of extraordinary scale, with sunken gardens, reflecting pools, and panoramic rooftop views over Marrakech. Browse the adjacent Mellah (Jewish Quarter) for its distinctive architecture and gold jewelry souks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a final luxury shopping experience in Marrakech's premium boutiques near the medina – curated argan oil beauty sets, hand-embroidered kaftans, bespoke leather goods, and artisan ceramics. Visit Atelier Nihal or 33 Rue Majorelle for high-end Moroccan design. Return to the resort for a final pool session, spa treatment, or simply relaxing on the beachfront terrace with a cocktail.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort's finest restaurant or a celebrated Marrakech establishment such as Nomad Rooftop or La Grande Table Marocaine at Royal Mansour – Morocco's most prestigious hotel restaurant. Toast to an unforgettable journey with Moroccan Champagne and a curated tasting menu. Private transfer to the airport for departure if flying out, or overnight at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Grand resort breakfast buffet – final indulgence with the full spread of Moroccan and international options, freshly squeezed juices, and specialty coffees.
meals.lunch: Chic lunch at a medina rooftop restaurant – grilled fish chermoula, Moroccan mezze, and fresh lemonade with orange blossom.
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner at La Grande Table Marocaine (Royal Mansour) or resort signature restaurant – chef's tasting menu with Moroccan wine pairing, featuring the finest interpretations of Moroccan haute cuisine in an opulent setting.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon activities. Book farewell dinner reservations at least 3 days in advance, especially for Royal Mansour. Arrange private airport transfer for departure. Allow extra time for last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks.
